diagnose.sql: SHOW GLOBAL STATUS WHERE Variable_name IN ('Threads_connected','Max_used_connections')

diagnose.look_for: the limit

diagnose.look_for: one app user holding many sleeping connections

diagnose.look_for: the limit

causes.title_en: The app opens connections and doesn't close them (many sleeping/idle ones)
causes.title_hi: App connection kholti hai par band nahi karti (bahut saare sleeping/idle)

causes.title_en: Real traffic is higher than the limit
causes.title_hi: Asli traffic limit se zyada hai

causes.title_en: Slow queries keep connections busy, so new requests pile up
causes.title_hi: Slow queries connection pakde rehti hain, nayi requests line mein lag jaati hain

fixes.steps_en: Lower wait_timeout (MySQL) / set idle_session_timeout (PostgreSQL 14+) so idle connections close; fix persistent connections in the app.
fixes.steps_hi: wait_timeout kam karo (MySQL) / idle_session_timeout set karo (PostgreSQL 14+) taaki idle connection band ho; app ke persistent connections theek karo.

fixes.steps_en: Raise max_connections carefully (each connection uses memory), or add a pooler (ProxySQL / PgBouncer).
fixes.steps_hi: max_connections dhyan se badhao (har connection memory leta hai), ya pooler lagao (ProxySQL / PgBouncer).

fixes.steps_en: Open the Live tab, find the slow queries and run them through the query fixer.
fixes.steps_hi: Live tab kholo, slow queries dhoondo aur unhe query fixer se theek karo.

verify.en: Threads_connected / active connections stay well under the limit for a day.
verify.hi: Ek din tak connections limit se kaafi neeche rahein.

diagnose.sql: SELECT GRANTEE, PRIVILEGE_TYPE, IS_GRANTABLE FROM information_schema.USER_PRIVILEGES ORDER BY GRANTEE
diagnose.look_for: accounts you don't know, '%' hosts (any computer), and SUPER / FILE / GRANT OPTION / CREATE USER given to app users

diagnose.sql: SELECT USER, HOST, DB, COMMAND, TIME FROM information_schema.PROCESSLIST ORDER BY TIME DESC
diagnose.look_for: sessions from an IP/host that isn't your app server or your office

diagnose.sql: SELECT TRIGGER_SCHEMA, TRIGGER_NAME, EVENT_MANIPULATION, EVENT_OBJECT_TABLE, ACTION_TIMING, CREATED, DEFINER, LEFT(ACTION_STATEMENT, 300) AS body FROM information_schema.TRIGGERS ORDER BY CREATED DESC
diagnose.look_for: a trigger nobody on your team made, especially on comments/users/usermeta/posts/orders, or one that writes into a users table

diagnose.sql: SELECT EVENT_SCHEMA, EVENT_NAME, DEFINER, STATUS, EVENT_TYPE, INTERVAL_VALUE, INTERVAL_FIELD, CREATED, LAST_EXECUTED, LEFT(EVENT_DEFINITION, 300) AS body FROM information_schema.EVENTS ORDER BY CREATED DESC
diagnose.look_for: scheduled events you didn't create (they can re-add a user, re-insert spam or delete data every few minutes)

diagnose.sql: SELECT ROUTINE_SCHEMA, ROUTINE_NAME, ROUTINE_TYPE, DEFINER, SECURITY_TYPE, CREATED, LAST_ALTERED FROM information_schema.ROUTINES WHERE ROUTINE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('sys', 'mysql') ORDER BY CREATED DESC
diagnose.look_for: procedures/functions with names you don't recognise, recently created, or with an unknown DEFINER

diagnose.sql: SELECT TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME, CREATE_TIME, TABLE_ROWS FROM information_schema.TABLES WHERE LOWER(TABLE_NAME) LIKE '%recover%' OR LOWER(TABLE_NAME) LIKE '%readme%' OR LOWER(TABLE_NAME) LIKE '%read_me%' OR LOWER(TABLE_NAME) LIKE '%warning%' OR LOWER(TABLE_NAME) LIKE '%bitcoin%' OR LOWER(TABLE_NAME) LIKE '%ransom%' OR LOWER(TABLE_NAME) LIKE '%hacked%' OR LOWER(TABLE_SCHEMA) LIKE '%recover%' OR LOWER(TABLE_SCHEMA) LIKE '%readme%' OR LOWER(TABLE_SCHEMA) LIKE '%read_me%'
diagnose.look_for: a table/database like RECOVER_YOUR_DATA, README, PLEASE_READ_ME or WARNING: that is the ransom note

diagnose.sql: SELECT TABLE_SCHEMA, TABLE_NAME, TABLE_ROWS, CREATE_TIME, UPDATE_TIME FROM information_schema.TABLES WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') ORDER BY CREATE_TIME DESC LIMIT 30
diagnose.look_for: tables created recently that nobody made, or important tables now with 0 rows

diagnose.sql: SHOW VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name IN ('bind_address', 'skip_networking', 'port', 'require_secure_transport', 'local_infile', 'secure_file_priv')
diagnose.look_for: bind_address 0.0.0.0 or * (open to every network), local_infile ON, secure_file_priv empty

diagnose.sql: SELECT rolname, rolsuper, rolcreaterole, rolcreatedb, rolcanlogin, rolreplication, rolbypassrls, rolvaliduntil FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname NOT LIKE 'pg\_%' ORDER BY rolsuper DESC, rolname
diagnose.look_for: a login role you don't know, or extra roles with superuser / createrole / bypassrls

diagnose.sql: SELECT g.rolname AS powerful_role, r.rolname AS member FROM pg_auth_members m JOIN pg_roles r ON r.oid = m.member JOIN pg_roles g ON g.oid = m.roleid WHERE g.rolname IN ('pg_execute_server_program', 'pg_read_server_files', 'pg_write_server_files', 'pg_signal_backend', 'pg_read_all_data', 'pg_write_all_data')
diagnose.look_for: an app or unknown role allowed to run server programs or read/write server files

diagnose.sql: SELECT usename, client_addr, application_name, backend_start, state FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE backend_type = 'client backend' ORDER BY backend_start
diagnose.look_for: connections from addresses that aren't your app or office, or a strange application_name

diagnose.sql: SELECT evtname, evtevent, evtowner::regrole AS owner, evtfoid::regproc AS runs_function, evtenabled FROM pg_event_trigger
diagnose.look_for: any event trigger you didn't create (they fire on CREATE/DROP/ALTER in the whole database)

diagnose.sql: SELECT t.tgrelid::regclass AS on_table, t.tgname, t.tgfoid::regproc AS runs_function, t.tgenabled FROM pg_trigger t WHERE NOT t.tgisinternal ORDER BY 1
diagnose.look_for: a trigger you don't know, especially one running a function you didn't write

diagnose.sql: SELECT table_schema, table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE lower(table_name) LIKE '%recover%' OR lower(table_name) LIKE '%readme%' OR lower(table_name) LIKE '%read_me%' OR lower(table_name) LIKE '%warning%' OR lower(table_name) LIKE '%bitcoin%' OR lower(table_name) LIKE '%ransom%' OR lower(table_name) LIKE '%hacked%'
diagnose.look_for: a ransom-note table (README, RECOVER_YOUR_DATA, WARNING...) in this database

diagnose.sql: SELECT datname, pg_database_size(datname) AS bytes FROM pg_database WHERE NOT datistemplate ORDER BY datname
diagnose.look_for: a new database like readme_to_recover, or your database suddenly tiny

diagnose.sql: SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name IN ('listen_addresses', 'port', 'ssl', 'password_encryption', 'log_connections', 'log_statement')
diagnose.look_for: listen_addresses '*' (open to every network), md5 passwords, connection logging off

causes.title_en: An account or permission exists that nobody on your team created
causes.title_hi: Koi account ya permission hai jo aapki team ne nahi banaya

causes.title_en: Triggers, scheduled events or procedures were planted to keep access or change data
causes.title_hi: Triggers, scheduled events ya procedures daale gaye hain taaki access bana rahe ya data badle

causes.title_en: Data was deleted and a ransom note left
causes.title_hi: Data delete karke ransom note chhoda gaya

causes.title_en: The database is open to the whole internet
causes.title_hi: Database poore internet ke liye khula hai

causes.title_en: Nothing suspicious found: the change came from a plugin, update or teammate
causes.title_hi: Kuch shak wala nahi mila: badlaav plugin, update ya team ke kisi member se aaya

fixes.steps_en: Treat it as a break-in: follow 'Hacked: what to do right now' (copy for evidence, change every password, remove the unknown account).
fixes.steps_hi: Ise break-in maano: 'Hack ho gaya: abhi turant kya karein' follow karo (saboot ke liye copy, har password badlo, anjaan account hatao).

fixes.steps_en: Open the 'unknown triggers' or 'unknown scheduled events/procedures' playbook and remove only what you have confirmed is not yours.
fixes.steps_hi: 'Anjaan triggers' ya 'anjaan scheduled events/procedures' playbook kholo aur sirf wahi hatao jo pakka aapka nahi hai.

fixes.steps_en: Don't pay. Follow the ransom-note playbook: keep the note as evidence, close access, restore from your backup.
fixes.steps_hi: Paise mat do. Ransom-note playbook follow karo: note saboot ke liye rakho, access band karo, backup se restore karo.

fixes.steps_en: Make the database listen only on the private network/localhost and allow its port only from your app server in the firewall.
fixes.steps_hi: Database ko sirf private network/localhost pe sunne do aur firewall mein port sirf app server ke liye kholo.

fixes.steps_en: Keep the check results; turn on connection/query logging so a real break-in would be visible next time.
fixes.steps_hi: Check ke results rakh lo; connection/query logging on karo taaki agli baar asli break-in dikh jaye.

verify.en: Every account, trigger, event and procedure in the results is known to your team, and no ransom table exists.
verify.hi: Results mein har account, trigger, event aur procedure aapki team ka jaana-pehchana hai, aur koi ransom table nahi hai.

diagnose.look_for: log_bin ON means the changes (and the attack) are recorded and can be replayed up to a point in time

diagnose.look_for: connections from addresses that aren't your app or office, or a strange application_name

causes.title_en: The attacker may still be connected or able to log in
causes.title_hi: Attacker abhi bhi connected ho sakta hai ya login kar sakta hai

causes.title_en: The database and app passwords must be treated as stolen
causes.title_hi: Database aur app ke passwords ko chori hua maano

causes.title_en: The database port is reachable from the internet
causes.title_hi: Database ka port internet se pahuncha ja sakta hai

fixes.steps_en: 1) Take a full copy (dump or disk snapshot) of the database AS IT IS now and keep it aside as evidence; don't clean before this. 2) Note the time you noticed it. 3) Put the site in maintenance mode so customers aren't served infected pages.
fixes.steps_hi: 1) Database ki abhi jaisi hai waisi poori copy (dump ya disk snapshot) lo aur saboot ke liye alag rakho; isse pehle safai mat karo. 2) Kab pata chala, time likh lo. 3) Site maintenance mode mein daalo taaki customers ko infected page na dikhe.

fixes.steps_en: Change the password of every database account (ALTER USER ... IDENTIFIED BY / ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD), put the new app password in the app config (wp-config.php, .env), change hosting/cPanel/SSH/FTP and admin-panel passwords, and replace the WordPress secret keys so every session is logged out.
fixes.steps_hi: Har database account ka password badlo (ALTER USER ... IDENTIFIED BY / ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD), naya app password config mein daalo (wp-config.php, .env), hosting/cPanel/SSH/FTP aur admin panel ke password badlo, aur WordPress secret keys badlo taaki sab log out ho jayein.

fixes.steps_en: Close the port to the internet now: bind the server to localhost/private IP (bind_address / listen_addresses), allow only your app server in the firewall, and remove accounts that can log in from any host ('%').
fixes.steps_hi: Port abhi internet ke liye band karo: server ko localhost/private IP pe bind karo (bind_address / listen_addresses), firewall mein sirf app server allow karo, aur jo account kisi bhi host ('%') se login kar sakte hain unhe hatao.

verify.en: Only your app and your team's known accounts are connected; old passwords no longer work; the port can't be reached from outside.
verify.hi: Sirf aapki app aur team ke jaane-pehchane account connected hain; purane password kaam nahi karte; bahar se port nahi khulta.

diagnose.sql: SELECT u.ID, u.user_login, u.display_name, u.user_registered FROM wp_users u JOIN wp_usermeta m ON m.user_id = u.ID WHERE m.meta_key LIKE '%capabilities' AND m.meta_value LIKE '%administrator%' ORDER BY u.user_registered DESC
diagnose.look_for: an administrator you don't know, or one 'registered' on an odd date (attackers often fake an old date)

diagnose.sql: SELECT m.user_id, m.meta_key, m.meta_value, u.user_login FROM wp_usermeta m LEFT JOIN wp_users u ON u.ID = m.user_id WHERE (m.meta_key LIKE '%capabilities' AND m.meta_value LIKE '%administrator%') OR (m.meta_key LIKE '%user_level' AND m.meta_value = '10')
diagnose.look_for: admin rights given to a user id that has no row in wp_users (user_login empty) or to a user you don't recognise

diagnose.sql: SELECT ID, user_login, display_name, user_registered FROM wp_users ORDER BY ID DESC LIMIT 20
diagnose.look_for: the newest user ids: a high id with an old registration date was added later and back-dated

diagnose.sql: SELECT option_name, LEFT(option_value, 200) AS value FROM wp_options WHERE option_name IN ('siteurl', 'home', 'admin_email', 'users_can_register', 'default_role', 'template', 'stylesheet')
diagnose.look_for: siteurl/home pointing to a strange domain, admin_email you don't own, users_can_register = 1 together with default_role = administrator

diagnose.sql: SELECT TRIGGER_SCHEMA, TRIGGER_NAME, EVENT_MANIPULATION, EVENT_OBJECT_TABLE, ACTION_TIMING, CREATED, DEFINER, LEFT(ACTION_STATEMENT, 300) AS body FROM information_schema.TRIGGERS ORDER BY CREATED DESC
diagnose.look_for: a trigger nobody on your team made, especially on comments/users/usermeta/posts/orders, or one that writes into a users table

diagnose.sql: SELECT EVENT_SCHEMA, EVENT_NAME, DEFINER, STATUS, EVENT_TYPE, INTERVAL_VALUE, INTERVAL_FIELD, CREATED, LAST_EXECUTED, LEFT(EVENT_DEFINITION, 300) AS body FROM information_schema.EVENTS ORDER BY CREATED DESC
diagnose.look_for: scheduled events you didn't create (they can re-add a user, re-insert spam or delete data every few minutes)

causes.title_en: An attacker added an administrator account
causes.title_hi: Attacker ne administrator account jod diya

causes.title_en: Admin rights were written straight into wp_usermeta (sometimes for a user id that isn't in wp_users)
causes.title_hi: Admin rights seedhe wp_usermeta mein likh diye (kabhi aise user id ke liye jo wp_users mein hai hi nahi)

causes.title_en: A trigger, event or infected file re-creates the admin after you delete it
causes.title_hi: Koi trigger, event ya infected file admin ko delete ke baad phir bana deti hai

causes.title_en: Anyone can register, and new users get the administrator role
causes.title_hi: Koi bhi register kar sakta hai, aur naye user ko administrator role milta hai

fixes.steps_en: After the evidence copy: in Users, delete the unknown admin and give its content to a real user (or delete its wp_users row and its wp_usermeta rows). Reset every real admin's password.
fixes.steps_hi: Saboot wali copy ke baad: Users mein anjaan admin delete karo aur uska content asli user ko do (ya wp_users ki row aur uski wp_usermeta rows hatao). Har asli admin ka password reset karo.

fixes.steps_en: Delete the wp_usermeta capability/user_level rows that give admin to unknown or missing user ids.
fixes.steps_hi: wp_usermeta ki woh capability/user_level rows hatao jo anjaan ya gayab user id ko admin banati hain.

fixes.steps_en: Remove the trigger/event first (see the triggers and events playbooks), replace WordPress core files with a fresh copy and scan themes/plugins; then delete the admin again.
fixes.steps_hi: Pehle trigger/event hatao (triggers aur events playbook dekho), WordPress core files fresh copy se badlo aur themes/plugins scan karo; phir admin dobara delete karo.

fixes.steps_en: Set users_can_register to 0 (or default_role back to subscriber) in Settings > General.
fixes.steps_hi: Settings > General mein users_can_register 0 karo (ya default_role wapas subscriber).

verify.en: The admin list holds only people you know, and stays that way after a day (nothing re-creates it).
verify.hi: Admin list mein sirf jaane-pehchane log hain, aur ek din baad bhi waisa hi hai (koi dobara nahi banata).

causes.title_en: An attacker created their own account to come back later
causes.title_hi: Attacker ne wapas aane ke liye apna account bana liya

causes.title_en: An existing app account was given admin powers (SUPER/FILE/GRANT, superuser, server-program roles)
causes.title_hi: Pehle wale app account ko admin powers de di gayi (SUPER/FILE/GRANT, superuser, server-program roles)

causes.title_en: An old account from a previous developer or tool, still active

fixes.steps_en: After the evidence copy: lock it first (ALTER USER ... ACCOUNT LOCK / ALTER ROLE ... NOLOGIN), end its sessions, then DROP USER / DROP ROLE (reassign or drop what it owns first in PostgreSQL).
fixes.steps_hi: Saboot wali copy ke baad: pehle lock karo (ALTER USER ... ACCOUNT LOCK / ALTER ROLE ... NOLOGIN), uske sessions band karo, phir DROP USER / DROP ROLE (PostgreSQL mein pehle uski cheezein reassign/drop karo).

fixes.steps_en: REVOKE the extra rights so the app user has only SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on its own database (ALTER ROLE ... NOSUPERUSER; REVOKE pg_execute_server_program ...), then change its password.
fixes.steps_hi: Extra rights REVOKE karo taaki app user ke paas sirf apne database pe SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE ho (ALTER ROLE ... NOSUPERUSER; REVOKE pg_execute_server_program ...), phir password badlo.

fixes.steps_en: Confirm with the team, then lock or drop it; keep one named account per person or app.
fixes.steps_hi: Team se confirm karo, phir lock ya drop karo; har insaan ya app ka ek apna naam wala account rakho.

verify.en: Every account and grant in the list is known, app accounts have only data rights, and no account allows any host ('%') unless needed.
verify.hi: List ka har account aur grant jaana-pehchana hai, app accounts ke paas sirf data rights hain, aur koi account bina zaroorat kisi bhi host ('%') se nahi aata.

diagnose.sql: SELECT TRIGGER_SCHEMA, TRIGGER_NAME, EVENT_MANIPULATION, EVENT_OBJECT_TABLE, ACTION_TIMING, CREATED, DEFINER, LEFT(ACTION_STATEMENT, 300) AS body FROM information_schema.TRIGGERS ORDER BY CREATED DESC

diagnose.sql: SELECT u.ID, u.user_login, u.display_name, u.user_registered FROM wp_users u JOIN wp_usermeta m ON m.user_id = u.ID WHERE m.meta_key LIKE '%capabilities' AND m.meta_value LIKE '%administrator%' ORDER BY u.user_registered DESC
diagnose.look_for: an administrator you don't know, or one 'registered' on an odd date (attackers often fake an old date)

diagnose.look_for: a trigger you don't know, especially one running a function you didn't write

diagnose.look_for: any event trigger you didn't create (they fire on CREATE/DROP/ALTER in the whole database)

diagnose.sql: SELECT n.nspname AS schema, p.proname AS function, r.rolname AS owner, l.lanname AS language, p.prosecdef AS security_definer FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = p.pronamespace JOIN pg_roles r ON r.oid = p.proowner JOIN pg_language l ON l.oid = p.prolang WHERE n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema') ORDER BY n.nspname, p.proname
diagnose.look_for: functions with odd names, written in C or an untrusted language (plpython3u, plperlu), or SECURITY DEFINER owned by a superuser

causes.title_en: A trigger fires on a normal action (new comment/order/user) and secretly adds an admin or changes data
causes.title_hi: Ek trigger normal kaam (naya comment/order/user) pe chalta hai aur chupke se admin banata ya data badalta hai

causes.title_en: (PostgreSQL) an event trigger fires on every CREATE/ALTER/DROP
causes.title_hi: (PostgreSQL) ek event trigger har CREATE/ALTER/DROP pe chalta hai

causes.title_en: The trigger belongs to a plugin, audit tool or your own app
causes.title_hi: Trigger kisi plugin, audit tool ya aapki apni app ka hai

fixes.steps_en: Save its definition (SHOW CREATE TRIGGER / pg_get_triggerdef) as evidence, then DROP TRIGGER it; drop the function it called (PostgreSQL) and undo what it created (users, rows).
fixes.steps_hi: Uski definition (SHOW CREATE TRIGGER / pg_get_triggerdef) saboot ke liye save karo, phir DROP TRIGGER karo; jo function woh chalata tha use hatao (PostgreSQL) aur jo usne banaya (users, rows) use undo karo.

fixes.steps_en: Save it, then DROP EVENT TRIGGER (needs a superuser) and check who owns it: that role is likely compromised too.
fixes.steps_hi: Save karo, phir DROP EVENT TRIGGER (superuser chahiye) aur dekho owner kaun hai: woh role bhi shayad compromised hai.

fixes.steps_en: Keep it; write down which plugin/app owns it so the next check is quick.
fixes.steps_hi: Rehne do; likh lo kaunse plugin/app ka hai taaki agla check jaldi ho.

verify.en: The trigger list has only triggers you can name the owner of, and new comments/orders no longer create users or change data.
verify.hi: Trigger list mein sirf woh triggers hain jinka owner aap bata sakte ho, aur naye comment/order ab user nahi banate na data badalte.

diagnose.sql: SELECT evtname, evtevent, evtowner::regrole AS owner, evtfoid::regproc AS runs_function, evtenabled FROM pg_event_trigger
diagnose.look_for: any event trigger you didn't create (they fire on CREATE/DROP/ALTER in the whole database)

causes.title_en: A scheduled event re-adds spam, users or deletes data on a timer
causes.title_hi: Ek scheduled event timer pe spam, users wapas daalta ya data delete karta hai

causes.title_en: A planted procedure/function (MySQL routine, PostgreSQL function in C or an untrusted language) gives the attacker a way back

fixes.steps_en: Save SHOW CREATE EVENT as evidence, ALTER EVENT ... DISABLE at once, then DROP EVENT; in PostgreSQL unschedule the pg_cron job.

fixes.steps_en: Save its code, DROP PROCEDURE/FUNCTION, and check its DEFINER/owner account: lock that account and change its password. Drop untrusted languages you don't use.

fixes.steps_en: Keep it and note its owner.
fixes.steps_hi: Rehne do aur uska owner likh lo.

verify.en: No unknown events/routines are left, and the spam or data change doesn't come back at the next scheduled time.
verify.hi: Koi anjaan event/routine nahi bacha, aur agle scheduled time pe spam ya data badlaav wapas nahi aata.

diagnose.look_for: a trigger nobody on your team made, especially on comments/users/usermeta/posts/orders, or one that writes into a users table

diagnose.sql: SELECT EVENT_SCHEMA, EVENT_NAME, DEFINER, STATUS, EVENT_TYPE, INTERVAL_VALUE, INTERVAL_FIELD, CREATED, LAST_EXECUTED, LEFT(EVENT_DEFINITION, 300) AS body FROM information_schema.EVENTS ORDER BY CREATED DESC
diagnose.look_for: scheduled events you didn't create (they can re-add a user, re-insert spam or delete data every few minutes)

causes.title_en: A script/link was added to many existing posts at once
causes.title_hi: Bahut saare purane posts mein ek saath script/link jod diya gaya

causes.title_en: The attacker created many new spam pages/posts
causes.title_hi: Attacker ne bahut saare naye spam pages/posts bana diye

causes.title_en: Something keeps putting it back (infected file, trigger or event)
causes.title_hi: Koi cheez ise wapas daalti rehti hai (infected file, trigger ya event)

fixes.steps_en: Best: restore posts from a clean backup taken before the injection day. Otherwise remove the exact injected snippet from the affected rows after approval (we show every changed row; Undo keeps the old text). Don't run a blind search-replace on serialized data in wp_options/wp_postmeta: it breaks it.
fixes.steps_hi: Sabse accha: injection wale din se pehle ke saaf backup se posts restore karo. Warna approval ke baad affected rows se wahi daala gaya code hatao (har badli row dikhegi; Undo purana text rakhta hai). wp_options/wp_postmeta ke serialized data pe andha search-replace mat chalao: woh toot jata hai.

fixes.steps_en: Delete the spam posts by the date range/author they share (after reviewing the list), then ask Google to re-crawl and remove them from search.
fixes.steps_hi: List dekh ke, spam posts ko unki common date range/author se delete karo, phir Google se re-crawl karwao taaki search se hatein.

fixes.steps_en: Remove the source first: replace core files, scan themes/plugins, and check the triggers/events playbooks; otherwise the cleaning is undone.
fixes.steps_hi: Pehle jad hatao: core files badlo, themes/plugins scan karo, aur triggers/events playbook dekho; warna safai phir se bekaar ho jayegi.

verify.en: The check finds no injected script/link in posts, the spam page count is back to normal, and it stays clean for a few days.
verify.hi: Check ko posts mein koi daala hua script/link nahi milta, spam pages normal ho gaye, aur kuch din tak saaf rehta hai.

fixes.steps_en: Treat the whole server as compromised: take the evidence copy, cut it off the internet (listen_addresses, pg_hba.conf, firewall), change all role passwords to strong ones with scram-sha-256, remove unknown roles, and ask your host/admin to clean the OS (kill the miner, check cron and startup files) or rebuild the server and restore the data from a clean backup.

fixes.steps_en: ALTER ROLE app NOSUPERUSER; REVOKE pg_execute_server_program / pg_read_server_files / pg_write_server_files FROM the app role; apps never need them.

causes.title_en: You need a backup taken before the first sign of the break-in
causes.title_hi: Break-in ke pehle nishaan se pehle ka backup chahiye

causes.title_en: The backup you restored already contained the backdoor (user, trigger, event, injected content)

fixes.steps_en: Find the earliest sign (oldest unknown admin, first injected post, trigger CREATED time). Restore the backup from before that date into a NEW database first, run the hacked checks on it, then switch the app to it. With binlog/WAL you can replay up to just before the attack (point-in-time recovery). Orders/sign-ups made after the backup must be copied over by hand.
fixes.steps_hi: Sabse pehla nishaan dhoondo (sabse purana anjaan admin, pehla infected post, trigger ka CREATED time). Us date se pehle ka backup pehle ek NAYE database mein restore karo, us pe hacked checks chalao, phir app ko us pe shift karo. binlog/WAL ho to attack se theek pehle tak replay ho sakta hai (point-in-time recovery). Backup ke baad ke orders/sign-ups haath se copy karne honge.

fixes.steps_en: Pick an older backup, or clean the restored copy with the triggers/events/admin/spam playbooks before going live. And close the way in, or it will happen again.
fixes.steps_hi: Aur purana backup lo, ya live karne se pehle restored copy ko triggers/events/admin/spam playbooks se saaf karo. Aur andar aane ka raasta band karo, warna phir hoga.

fixes.steps_en: Ask your hosting provider for their snapshots; otherwise clean the current database in place with the playbooks. Then set up daily backups stored away from the server and test a restore.
fixes.steps_hi: Hosting provider se unke snapshots maango; warna playbooks se current database ko wahin saaf karo. Phir roz ka backup server se alag jagah rakho aur restore test karo.

verify.en: The restored database passes all the hacked checks (no unknown admins, triggers, events, spam) and the site works with today's real data copied in.
verify.hi: Restored database saare hacked checks pass karta hai (koi anjaan admin, trigger, event, spam nahi) aur aaj ka asli data copy karke site chal rahi hai.

fixes.steps_hi: Hack ke time ka web server access log dekh ke page dhundo aur uska code prepared statements (parameterised queries) wala karo. SQL injection playbook dekho.

fixes.steps_en: Block public access to config/backup files, remove backups and .git from the web folder, then change the database password and update the app config.
fixes.steps_hi: Config/backup files ka public access band karo, web folder se backups aur .git hatao, phir database password badlo aur app config update karo.

fixes.steps_en: Give every database account a long unique password (a password manager can generate it) and turn on a password-strength check.
fixes.steps_hi: Har database account ko lamba aur alag password do (password manager bana dega) aur password-strength check on karo.

fixes.steps_en: Make the database listen only on localhost/private network and allow the port only from your app server in the firewall.
fixes.steps_hi: Database ko sirf localhost/private network par sunne do aur firewall mein port sirf app server ke liye kholo.

fixes.steps_en: Update the CMS, plugins, themes and admin tools; remove the ones you don't use (especially an old phpMyAdmin on a public URL).
fixes.steps_hi: CMS, plugins, themes aur admin tools update karo; jo use nahi hote unhe hatao (khaas kar public URL par pada purana phpMyAdmin).

fixes.steps_en: Give the app its own user with only SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on its own database (no FILE, SUPER, GRANT or superuser).

diagnose.sql: SELECT usename, client_addr, application_name, backend_start, state FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE backend_type = 'client backend' ORDER BY client_addr
diagnose.look_for: the app's role connected from an address that is not the app server

diagnose.sql: SELECT rolname, rolsuper, rolcreaterole, rolcreatedb, rolcanlogin FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user
diagnose.look_for: how powerful the leaked role is (superuser = the whole server is exposed)

causes.title_en: Config or .env file readable through the web server (wrong document root, missing deny rule)
causes.title_hi: Config ya .env file web server se padhi ja sakti thi (galat document root, deny rule nahi)

causes.title_en: A database dump or config copy (wp-config.php.bak, db.sql, site.zip) left in a public folder
causes.title_hi: Database dump ya config ki copy (wp-config.php.bak, db.sql, site.zip) public folder mein chhodi

causes.title_en: Password committed to a git repository or shared in chat/email
causes.title_hi: Password git repo mein commit hua ya chat/email mein share hua

causes.title_en: Debug/error page shows environment variables or connection details
causes.title_hi: Debug/error page environment variables ya connection details dikhata hai

fixes.steps_en: Change the database password now and update the app config; deny web access to .env/config files (keep them outside the public folder).
fixes.steps_hi: Abhi database password badlo aur app config update karo; .env/config files ka web access band karo (unhe public folder ke bahar rakho).

fixes.steps_en: Delete backups and archives from public folders, store them off the web server, then change every password they contain.
fixes.steps_hi: Public folders se backups aur archives hatao, unhe web server ke bahar rakho, phir unme likhe har password ko badlo.

fixes.steps_en: Treat the password as public forever: change it, remove it from the repo history with the git host's guidance, and use environment secrets instead.
fixes.steps_hi: Password ko hamesha ke liye public maano: badlo, git host ke tarike se repo history se hatao, aur environment secrets use karo.

fixes.steps_en: Turn debug mode off in production (APP_DEBUG=false, WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY off) and change the password that was shown.
fixes.steps_hi: Production mein debug mode band karo (APP_DEBUG=false, WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY off) aur jo password dikha use badlo.

verify.en: The old password no longer works, the config file returns 403/404 from the browser, and no connections come from unknown hosts.
verify.hi: Purana password ab kaam nahi karta, browser mein config file 403/404 deti hai, aur anjaan host se koi connection nahi aata.

test_phrases: our config file with the db login was open on the internet
hamari config file mein db ka login tha aur wo internet pe khuli padi thi
हमारी कॉन्फ़िग फाइल जिसमें डीबी का लॉगिन था वो इंटरनेट पर खुली थी

title_en: Someone keeps trying to guess the database password (failed logins)
title_hi: Koi baar baar database ka password guess karne ki koshish kar raha hai (failed logins)
symptoms: lots of failed login attempts on mysql
access denied for user root many times in the error log
password authentication failed for user postgres again and again in logs
bots trying to log in to my database
error log mein baar baar access denied aa raha hai anjaan IP se
koi password guess kar raha hai database ka
brute force attack on database port
हज़ारों बार गलत पासवर्ड से लॉगिन की कोशिश
कोई डेटाबेस का पासवर्ड गेस कर रहा है
unknown IPs hammering port 3306
postgres log full of failed authentication from china russia
har second login fail ki entries aa rahi hain
unknown machines keep trying different passwords on the database
someone trying password after password on the db
anjaan computer baar baar password try kar rahe hain
koi lagataar galat password daal ke login try kar raha hai
रात भर कोई डेटाबेस पर पासवर्ड पर पासवर्ड आज़मा रहा है
अनजान मशीनें बार बार लॉगिन की कोशिश कर रही हैं
endless login attempts all night from strange addresses

diagnose.sql: SELECT IP, HOST, SUM_CONNECT_ERRORS, COUNT_AUTHENTICATION_ERRORS, FIRST_SEEN, LAST_SEEN FROM performance_schema.host_cache ORDER BY COUNT_AUTHENTICATION_ERRORS DESC LIMIT 20
diagnose.look_for: IPs with many authentication errors that are not yours

diagnose.sql: SHOW GLOBAL STATUS WHERE Variable_name IN ('Aborted_connects', 'Access_denied_errors', 'Connection_errors_internal', 'Connection_errors_max_connections')
diagnose.look_for: Aborted_connects / Access_denied_errors climbing fast between two checks = ongoing guessing

diagnose.sql: SHOW VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name IN ('bind_address', 'skip_networking', 'max_connect_errors', 'log_warnings', 'log_error_verbosity')
diagnose.look_for: listening on all addresses makes guessing possible; low log verbosity hides the failed logins

diagnose.sql: SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name IN ('listen_addresses', 'log_connections', 'password_encryption', 'authentication_timeout')
diagnose.look_for: listen_addresses '*' and log_connections off: guesses can happen and you can't see them

diagnose.sql: SELECT rolname, rolsuper, rolcanlogin, rolvaliduntil FROM pg_roles WHERE rolcanlogin ORDER BY rolsuper DESC, rolname
diagnose.look_for: accounts that can log in: the 'postgres' superuser with a password reachable from the internet is the usual target

causes.title_en: Database port reachable from the internet, so bots find it within hours
causes.title_hi: Database port internet se pahunch mein hai, bots kuch ghanton mein dhundh lete hain

causes.title_en: Common user names (root, postgres, admin) with password logins allowed from anywhere
causes.title_hi: Aam usernames (root, postgres, admin) ka password login kahin se bhi allowed

fixes.steps_en: Close the port in the firewall for everyone except your app server/VPN; bind the database to localhost or the private network.
fixes.steps_hi: Firewall mein port sabke liye band karo, sirf app server/VPN ke liye kholo; database ko localhost ya private network par bind karo.

fixes.steps_en: Disable remote login for root/postgres, use long unique passwords (scram-sha-256 on PostgreSQL), and check logs for a successful login from the same IPs.
fixes.steps_hi: root/postgres ka remote login band karo, lambe alag passwords rakho (PostgreSQL par scram-sha-256), aur logs mein dekho ki unhi IPs se koi login safal to nahi hua.

verify.en: Failed-login counters stop growing and the port is not reachable from outside (test from a phone hotspot).
verify.hi: Failed-login counters badhna band ho jaate hain aur port bahar se nahi khulta (phone hotspot se test karo).

test_phrases: random computers keep trying passwords on my db all night
raat bhar anjaan computers mere db pe password try karte rehte hain
रात भर अनजान कंप्यूटर मेरे डेटाबेस पर पासवर्ड आज़माते रहते हैं

title_en: Weak, default or reused database passwords
title_hi: Database ke kamzor, default ya dobara use hue passwords
symptoms: database password is too simple
root user has no password
we use the same password everywhere including the database
db ka password 123456 hai kya ye safe hai
root ka password khali hai
sab jagah ek hi password use karte hain
how to enforce strong passwords in mysql
postgres password still the default one
डेटाबेस का पासवर्ड बहुत आसान है
रूट यूज़र का कोई पासवर्ड नहीं है
password policy for database users
developer ne password admin123 rakha tha
my database password is just our company name and some numbers
db ka password bas naam aur 123 hai
password bahut aasaan rakha hai db login ka
is a password like company123 safe for the db
पासवर्ड बस कंपनी का नाम और कुछ नंबर है
डीबी लॉगिन का पासवर्ड बहुत आसान है

diagnose.sql: SHOW VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name LIKE 'validate_password%' OR Variable_name LIKE 'simple_password_check%' OR Variable_name LIKE 'cracklib_password_check%'
diagnose.look_for: empty result = no password-strength check is active on this server

diagnose.sql: SELECT PLUGIN_NAME, PLUGIN_STATUS, PLUGIN_TYPE FROM information_schema.PLUGINS WHERE PLUGIN_TYPE = 'PASSWORD VALIDATION' OR PLUGIN_NAME LIKE '%password%'
diagnose.look_for: which password plugins are loaded (mysql_native_password is old and weak; caching_sha2_password / ed25519 are stronger)

diagnose.sql: SELECT GRANTEE, PRIVILEGE_TYPE FROM information_schema.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE PRIVILEGE_TYPE IN ('SUPER', 'CREATE USER', 'FILE', 'SHUTDOWN') ORDER BY GRANTEE
diagnose.look_for: every admin-level account must have a strong unique password (an admin user sees all accounts here)

diagnose.sql: SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name IN ('password_encryption', 'listen_addresses')
diagnose.look_for: password_encryption md5 is the old method; scram-sha-256 is the safe one

diagnose.sql: SELECT rolname, rolsuper, rolcanlogin, rolvaliduntil FROM pg_roles WHERE rolcanlogin AND rolname NOT LIKE 'pg\_%' ORDER BY rolsuper DESC
diagnose.look_for: login roles to rotate; superusers first

causes.title_en: Short, common or default passwords (empty root, 'postgres', 'admin123')
causes.title_hi: Chhote, aam ya default passwords (khali root, 'postgres', 'admin123')

causes.title_en: The same password used for the database, hosting panel, email and WordPress
causes.title_hi: Database, hosting panel, email aur WordPress mein ek hi password

causes.title_en: Old password hashing (mysql_native_password / md5)
causes.title_hi: Purana password hashing (mysql_native_password / md5)

fixes.steps_en: Set a long random password for every account (ALTER USER ... IDENTIFIED BY / ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD) and turn on the password validation component/plugin.
fixes.steps_hi: Har account ka lamba random password set karo (ALTER USER ... IDENTIFIED BY / ALTER ROLE ... PASSWORD) aur password validation component/plugin on karo.

fixes.steps_en: Give each system its own password stored in a password manager; change the database one first, then the others.
fixes.steps_hi: Har system ka alag password password manager mein rakho; pehle database wala badlo, phir baaki.

fixes.steps_en: PostgreSQL: set password_encryption = scram-sha-256 and reset passwords, then use scram-sha-256 in pg_hba.conf. MySQL 8: move users to caching_sha2_password.
fixes.steps_hi: PostgreSQL: password_encryption = scram-sha-256 karo aur passwords reset karo, phir pg_hba.conf mein scram-sha-256. MySQL 8: users ko caching_sha2_password par le jao.

verify.en: A password-strength check is active, every login account has a new unique password, and the app still connects.
verify.hi: Password-strength check chalu hai, har login account ka naya alag password hai, aur app abhi bhi connect hota hai.

test_phrases: my db login is just the company name with 123, is that a problem
mera db login bas company ka naam aur 123 hai, kya ye galat hai
मेरे डेटाबेस का पासवर्ड बस कंपनी का नाम और 123 है, क्या ये ठीक है

title_en: Database is open to the whole internet (port 3306/5432 exposed)
title_hi: Database poore internet ke liye khula hai (port 3306/5432 khula)
symptoms: port 3306 is open to the internet
postgres 5432 publicly accessible
can anyone connect to my database from outside
database bahar se connect ho jata hai kisi bhi computer se
bind address 0.0.0.0 kar diya tha remote access ke liye
listen_addresses star kar diya hai
security scan says mysql port exposed
क्या कोई भी बाहर से मेरे डेटाबेस से जुड़ सकता है
डेटाबेस का पोर्ट इंटरनेट पर खुला है
shodan shows my database
remote mysql allow kar diya hai sab IP ke liye
how to stop outside access to my db server
anyone online can reach my db server
internet se koi bhi database server tak pahunch jata hai
database server sabke liye khula hai internet pe
इंटरनेट से कोई भी डेटाबेस सर्वर तक पहुंच जाता है
outsiders can connect straight to my database machine

diagnose.sql: SHOW VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name IN ('bind_address', 'skip_networking', 'port', 'require_secure_transport')
diagnose.look_for: bind_address 0.0.0.0, :: or * with no firewall means the whole internet can try to log in

diagnose.sql: SELECT GRANTEE, PRIVILEGE_TYPE FROM information_schema.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE GRANTEE LIKE '%@''\%''' ORDER BY GRANTEE
diagnose.look_for: accounts allowed from any host ('%'): together with an open port these are reachable by anyone

diagnose.sql: SELECT HOST, COUNT(*) AS connections FROM information_schema.PROCESSLIST GROUP BY HOST ORDER BY connections DESC
diagnose.look_for: client hosts that are not localhost/your app server

diagnose.sql: SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name IN ('listen_addresses', 'port', 'ssl')
diagnose.look_for: listen_addresses '*' listens on every network card

diagnose.sql: SELECT client_addr, count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE client_addr IS NOT NULL GROUP BY client_addr ORDER BY 2 DESC
diagnose.look_for: public IP addresses that are not yours

causes.title_en: The database listens on all network interfaces (bind_address / listen_addresses)
causes.title_hi: Database sabhi network interfaces par sunta hai (bind_address / listen_addresses)

causes.title_en: No firewall / security group rule limiting the port
causes.title_hi: Port ko limit karne wala koi firewall / security group rule nahi

causes.title_en: Accounts allowed from any host ('user'@'%' or 0.0.0.0/0 in pg_hba.conf)
causes.title_hi: Accounts har host se allowed ('user'@'%' ya pg_hba.conf mein 0.0.0.0/0)

fixes.steps_en: Set bind_address=127.0.0.1 (or the private IP) / listen_addresses='localhost' (or private IP) and restart in a quiet hour.
fixes.steps_hi: bind_address=127.0.0.1 (ya private IP) / listen_addresses='localhost' (ya private IP) karo aur shant time par restart karo.

fixes.steps_en: Allow the port only from the app server or your VPN in the firewall/cloud security group; for remote work use an SSH tunnel.
fixes.steps_hi: Firewall/cloud security group mein port sirf app server ya VPN ke liye kholo; bahar se kaam ke liye SSH tunnel use karo.

fixes.steps_en: Recreate accounts for the exact app host (user@'10.0.0.5') and replace 0.0.0.0/0 lines in pg_hba.conf with the app's address.
fixes.steps_hi: Accounts ko exact app host ke liye banao (user@'10.0.0.5') aur pg_hba.conf ki 0.0.0.0/0 lines ko app ke address se badlo.

verify.en: From a network outside yours, connecting to the port times out, and the app still works.
verify.hi: Aapke network ke bahar se port par connect karne par timeout aata hai, aur app phir bhi chalta hai.

test_phrases: anybody on the internet can reach my database server is that bad
internet pe koi bhi mere database server tak pahunch sakta hai kya
इंटरनेट पर कोई भी मेरे डेटाबेस सर्वर तक पहुंच सकता है

title_en: root / postgres superuser can log in from anywhere
title_hi: root / postgres superuser kahin se bhi login kar sakta hai
symptoms: root can login remotely
root@% exists in mysql
remote root access enabled
website uses the root user to connect to the database
app root user se chal raha hai database mein
root ka login bahar se ho jata hai
postgres superuser login from outside allowed
रूट यूज़र बाहर से लॉगिन हो जाता है
वेबसाइट रूट यूज़र से डेटाबेस चलाती है
how to disable remote root login mysql
superuser use kar rahe hain app ke liye
the top admin login of the database works from any machine
database ka sabse bada admin login har jagah se chalta hai
main admin account kisi bhi computer se login ho jata hai
डेटाबेस का सबसे बड़ा एडमिन लॉगिन किसी भी मशीन से चलता है
मुख्य एडमिन अकाउंट हर कंप्यूटर से खुल जाता है
master database account usable from anywhere

diagnose.sql: SELECT GRANTEE, PRIVILEGE_TYPE, IS_GRANTABLE FROM information_schema.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE GRANTEE LIKE '''root''@%' AND GRANTEE NOT LIKE '%@''localhost''' AND GRANTEE NOT LIKE '%@''127.0.0.1''' AND GRANTEE NOT LIKE '%@''::1''' ORDER BY GRANTEE
diagnose.look_for: any row = root can log in from a non-local host (an admin user sees all accounts here)

diagnose.sql: SELECT CURRENT_USER() AS connected_as
diagnose.look_for: if the app connects as root, every bug in the app becomes a full server takeover

diagnose.sql: SELECT rolname, rolsuper, rolcanlogin FROM pg_roles WHERE rolsuper AND rolcanlogin ORDER BY rolname
diagnose.look_for: superusers that can log in; only 'postgres' (local only) should be here

diagnose.sql: SELECT current_user, (SELECT rolsuper FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user) AS is_superuser
diagnose.look_for: the app must not connect as a superuser

causes.title_en: root/superuser allowed from any host for convenience during setup
causes.title_hi: Setup ke time suvidha ke liye root/superuser ko har host se allow kar diya

causes.title_en: The application connects with the root/superuser account
causes.title_hi: Application root/superuser account se connect hoti hai

fixes.steps_en: Remove the non-local root accounts (DROP USER 'root'@'%') after confirming a local admin login works; in pg_hba.conf allow postgres only via local/peer.
fixes.steps_hi: Local admin login chalne ki pushti ke baad non-local root accounts hatao (DROP USER 'root'@'%'); pg_hba.conf mein postgres ko sirf local/peer se allow karo.

fixes.steps_en: Create a dedicated app user with rights only on its own database, switch the app config to it, then change the root password.
fixes.steps_hi: App ke liye alag user banao jiske rights sirf uske database par hon, app config usme badlo, phir root ka password badlo.

verify.en: No root/superuser row from a remote host remains, and the app runs as its own limited user.
verify.hi: Remote host wali koi root/superuser entry nahi bachi, aur app apne limited user se chalti hai.

test_phrases: the main admin account of the database can be used from any computer
database ka main admin account kisi bhi computer se chal jata hai
डेटाबेस का मेन एडमिन अकाउंट किसी भी कंप्यूटर से चल जाता है

title_en: The app's database user has more rights than it needs (least privilege)
title_hi: App ke database user ke paas zarurat se zyada rights hain (least privilege)
symptoms: app user has all privileges on all databases
grant all on *.* to the website user
how to create a least privilege user for my app
website ke user ko saare rights de rakhe hain
ek hi user se saari websites chal rahi hain
app user ko kitni permission deni chahiye
limit what the application database account can do
वेबसाइट के यूज़र को सारे अधिकार दे रखे हैं
ऐप वाले डेटाबेस यूज़र को कितनी परमिशन चाहिए
one database user shared by all my client sites
remove drop and grant permission from app user
the account my site connects with has unlimited power
website wala db login sab kuch kar sakta hai, kuch bhi delete kar sakta hai
site ke login ke paas poore server ki power hai
वेबसाइट वाले लॉगिन के पास पूरी पावर है, कुछ भी कर सकता है
app ka login har cheez badal sakta hai
my website's db account can do whatever it wants

diagnose.sql: SELECT GRANTEE, PRIVILEGE_TYPE, IS_GRANTABLE FROM information_schema.USER_PRIVILEGES ORDER BY GRANTEE, PRIVILEGE_TYPE
diagnose.look_for: global rights (ON *.*) for the app user, especially SUPER, FILE, PROCESS, CREATE USER, GRANT OPTION, SHUTDOWN

diagnose.sql: SELECT GRANTEE, TABLE_SCHEMA, PRIVILEGE_TYPE, IS_GRANTABLE FROM information_schema.SCHEMA_PRIVILEGES ORDER BY GRANTEE, TABLE_SCHEMA
diagnose.look_for: the app user should appear only on its own database; DROP, GRANT OPTION, ALTER ROUTINE, EVENT, TRIGGER are rarely needed at run time

diagnose.sql: SELECT rolname, rolsuper, rolcreaterole, rolcreatedb, rolreplication, rolbypassrls FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user
diagnose.look_for: the app role should have all of these false

diagnose.sql: SELECT d.datname, pg_get_userbyid(d.datdba) AS owner FROM pg_database d WHERE NOT d.datistemplate ORDER BY 1
diagnose.look_for: if the app role owns the database it can change or drop anything; a separate owner role is safer

diagnose.sql: SELECT r.rolname AS member, g.rolname AS member_of FROM pg_auth_members m JOIN pg_roles r ON r.oid = m.member JOIN pg_roles g ON g.oid = m.roleid ORDER BY 1, 2
diagnose.look_for: membership in powerful roles (pg_read_server_files, pg_write_server_files, pg_execute_server_program, pg_read_all_data)

causes.title_en: App user created with ALL PRIVILEGES on *.* (or as superuser) during setup
causes.title_hi: Setup ke time app user ko *.* par ALL PRIVILEGES (ya superuser) de diya

causes.title_en: One user shared by several sites/apps, so one hacked site exposes all
causes.title_hi: Kai sites/apps ka ek hi user, to ek site hack hui to sab khul jaati hain

fixes.steps_en: Create a new app user with SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on its own database only (plus what migrations need, from a separate deploy user), switch the app to it, then remove the old rights.
fixes.steps_hi: Naya app user banao jiske paas sirf apne database par SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ho (migrations ke liye alag deploy user), app usme switch karo, phir purane rights hatao.

fixes.steps_en: Give each site its own user and its own password; keep a separate admin account that the websites never use.
fixes.steps_hi: Har site ka apna user aur apna password do; ek alag admin account rakho jo websites kabhi use na karein.

verify.en: The app user's rights list shows only its own database and data rights, and the site works normally.
verify.hi: App user ki rights list mein sirf uska database aur data wale rights dikhte hain, aur site normal chalti hai.

test_phrases: the login my website uses can do absolutely anything on the server
website jis login se chalti hai wo server pe kuch bhi kar sakta hai
वेबसाइट जिस लॉगिन से चलती है वो सर्वर पर कुछ भी कर सकता है

title_en: The database can read or write files on the server (FILE privilege, secure_file_priv, COPY PROGRAM)
title_hi: Database server ki files padh ya likh sakta hai (FILE privilege, secure_file_priv, COPY PROGRAM)
symptoms: secure_file_priv is empty
mysql user has FILE privilege
hacker wrote a php file through mysql
database se server pe file ban gayi
kisi ne mysql se shell file likh di
copy program used by attacker in postgres
load data local infile security risk
डेटाबेस से सर्वर पर फाइल बन गई
can the database user read my server files
into outfile se backdoor bana diya
postgres se server pe command chal gayi
a suspicious php file showed up in my site folder created by mysql
unknown file appeared in public_html and the database seems to have made it
site folder mein anjaan file aayi jo database ne likhi
ajeeb file ban gayi website folder mein database ki taraf se
डेटाबेस ने वेबसाइट फोल्डर में अजीब फाइल बना दी
वेबसाइट फोल्डर में अनजान फाइल आ गई

diagnose.sql: SHOW VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name IN ('secure_file_priv', 'local_infile')
diagnose.look_for: secure_file_priv empty = the server may read/write files anywhere it has OS access; NULL or a fixed folder is safe; local_infile ON lets clients load local files

diagnose.sql: SELECT GRANTEE, PRIVILEGE_TYPE FROM information_schema.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE PRIVILEGE_TYPE = 'FILE' ORDER BY GRANTEE
diagnose.look_for: only an admin should have FILE; an app user with FILE can drop files into the web folder

diagnose.sql: SELECT r.rolname AS member, g.rolname AS powerful_role FROM pg_auth_members m JOIN pg_roles r ON r.oid = m.member JOIN pg_roles g ON g.oid = m.roleid WHERE g.rolname IN ('pg_read_server_files', 'pg_write_server_files', 'pg_execute_server_program')
diagnose.look_for: members of these roles can read/write server files or run programs, like a superuser

diagnose.sql: SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles WHERE rolsuper AND rolcanlogin
diagnose.look_for: superusers can run server programs through COPY ... PROGRAM; keep them few and local

causes.title_en: MySQL: FILE privilege given to app users and secure_file_priv not limited
causes.title_hi: MySQL: app users ko FILE privilege diya aur secure_file_priv limit nahi

causes.title_en: PostgreSQL: superuser or server-file roles given to an app or remote role
causes.title_hi: PostgreSQL: app ya remote role ko superuser ya server-file roles diye

fixes.steps_en: Set secure_file_priv to NULL or a private folder (needs restart), set local_infile=OFF, and REVOKE FILE ON *.* from every non-admin user (approved change). Then search the web folder for files the database wrote.
fixes.steps_hi: secure_file_priv ko NULL ya private folder karo (restart chahiye), local_infile=OFF karo, aur har non-admin user se FILE ON *.* REVOKE karo (approved change). Phir web folder mein database ki likhi files dhundo.

fixes.steps_en: Remove those role memberships and superuser from app roles (ALTER ROLE ... NOSUPERUSER), then check the server for unknown processes and cron jobs.
fixes.steps_hi: App roles se ye memberships aur superuser hatao (ALTER ROLE ... NOSUPERUSER), phir server par anjaan processes aur cron jobs dekho.

verify.en: secure_file_priv is limited, no app user has FILE or server-file roles, and no unknown files appear in the web folder.
verify.hi: secure_file_priv limited hai, kisi app user ke paas FILE ya server-file roles nahi, aur web folder mein koi anjaan file nahi aati.

test_phrases: a strange php file appeared in my website folder and it seems the database created it

how to enable ssl for mysql connections
postgres ssl off

डेटाबेस के लिए SSL कैसे चालू करें
tls for database traffic between servers
compliance audit asks for encryption in transit for the db

diagnose.sql: SHOW VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name IN ('have_ssl', 'have_openssl', 'require_secure_transport', 'tls_version', 'ssl_cert')
diagnose.look_for: have_ssl DISABLED / no certificate = connections cannot be encrypted; require_secure_transport OFF = plain connections are allowed

diagnose.sql: SHOW SESSION STATUS WHERE Variable_name IN ('Ssl_cipher', 'Ssl_version')
diagnose.look_for: an empty Ssl_cipher means this very connection is not encrypted

diagnose.sql: SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name IN ('ssl', 'ssl_min_protocol_version', 'listen_addresses')
diagnose.look_for: ssl off means every remote login and query travels in plain text

diagnose.sql: SELECT s.pid, a.usename, a.client_addr, s.ssl, s.version FROM pg_stat_ssl s JOIN pg_stat_activity a ON a.pid = s.pid WHERE a.client_addr IS NOT NULL
diagnose.look_for: remote connections with ssl = false

causes.title_en: The server has no certificate configured / SSL turned off
causes.title_hi: Server par certificate set nahi / SSL band

causes.title_en: SSL exists but clients are allowed to connect without it
causes.title_hi: SSL hai par clients bina uske bhi connect kar sakte hain

fixes.steps_en: Configure a certificate (ssl_cert/ssl_key in MySQL; ssl=on with server.crt/server.key in PostgreSQL) and restart in a quiet hour. Managed clouds: turn on 'require SSL' in the console.
fixes.steps_hi: Certificate set karo (MySQL mein ssl_cert/ssl_key; PostgreSQL mein ssl=on aur server.crt/server.key) aur shant time par restart karo. Managed cloud: console mein 'require SSL' on karo.

fixes.steps_en: Require it: require_secure_transport=ON (MySQL) or hostssl lines instead of host in pg_hba.conf (PostgreSQL); set the app's connection to sslmode=require / verify-full.
fixes.steps_hi: Zaroori banao: require_secure_transport=ON (MySQL) ya pg_hba.conf mein host ki jagah hostssl (PostgreSQL); app ke connection mein sslmode=require / verify-full.

verify.en: Ssl_cipher (MySQL) or pg_stat_ssl.ssl (PostgreSQL) shows encryption for the app's connection, and a plain connection is refused.
verify.hi: App ke connection ke liye Ssl_cipher (MySQL) ya pg_stat_ssl.ssl (PostgreSQL) encryption dikhata hai, aur bina SSL ka connection mana ho jata hai.

title_en: No record of who did what in the database (turn on audit / connection logging)
title_hi: Database mein kisne kya kiya iska koi record nahi (audit / connection logging on karo)
symptoms: how to know who changed data in my database
no logs of who logged in to the database
enable audit log mysql
pgaudit setup for tracking changes
kisne data badla pata kaise kare
database mein login ka record nahi hai
har query ka record rakhna hai

कौन कब लॉगिन हुआ उसका रिकॉर्ड चाहिए
auditor wants database activity logs
track all logins and changes made to the db
i want evidence of who modified the data and at what time
keep a trail of everyone who touches the database
record rakhna hai ki data kisne kab badla
saboot chahiye kisne kab data chheda
किसने कब डेटा बदला इसका सबूत चाहिए
डेटा कौन कब छेड़ता है उसका रिकॉर्ड रखना है
proof for the future of who changed what

diagnose.sql: SHOW VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name IN ('general_log', 'general_log_file', 'log_output', 'log_error', 'server_audit_logging', 'audit_log_file')
diagnose.look_for: general_log OFF and no audit plugin = no record of logins or statements

diagnose.sql: SELECT PLUGIN_NAME, PLUGIN_STATUS FROM information_schema.PLUGINS WHERE PLUGIN_NAME LIKE '%audit%'
diagnose.look_for: MariaDB server_audit or MySQL Enterprise audit_log loaded?

diagnose.sql: SHOW VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name IN ('log_bin', 'binlog_format', 'binlog_expire_logs_seconds', 'expire_logs_days')
diagnose.look_for: the binary log records every data change: needed to find and undo what an attacker changed

diagnose.sql: SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name IN ('log_connections', 'log_disconnections', 'log_statement', 'log_line_prefix', 'logging_collector', 'shared_preload_libraries')
diagnose.look_for: log_connections off and log_statement none = nothing to look back at; 'pgaudit' in shared_preload_libraries means auditing is available

causes.title_en: Default settings keep almost no history (general log off, connections not logged)
causes.title_hi: Default settings lagbhag koi history nahi rakhti (general log band, connections log nahi)

causes.title_en: Logs exist but are deleted too quickly or kept only on the same server
causes.title_hi: Logs hain par jaldi delete ho jaate hain ya sirf usi server par rakhe hain

fixes.steps_en: Log logins and changes, not everything: MariaDB server_audit plugin (CONNECT, QUERY_DDL, QUERY_DCL), MySQL audit plugin or binary log; PostgreSQL log_connections=on, log_disconnections=on, log_statement='ddl' (or pgaudit). Watch disk use.
fixes.steps_hi: Sab nahi, sirf logins aur changes log karo: MariaDB server_audit plugin (CONNECT, QUERY_DDL, QUERY_DCL), MySQL audit plugin ya binary log; PostgreSQL log_connections=on, log_disconnections=on, log_statement='ddl' (ya pgaudit). Disk par nazar rakho.

fixes.steps_en: Ship logs to another machine or log service and keep them at least 90 days, so an attacker can't wipe them.
fixes.steps_hi: Logs dusri machine ya log service par bhejo aur kam se kam 90 din rakho, taaki hacker unhe mita na sake.

verify.en: A test login and a test table change appear in the log, and the log is copied off the server.
verify.hi: Ek test login aur ek test table change log mein dikhta hai, aur log server ke bahar copy hota hai.

test_phrases: next time i want proof of who touched our data and when
agli baar saboot chahiye ki data ko kisne aur kab chheda
अगली बार सबूत चाहिए कि डेटा को किसने और कब छेड़ा

title_en: Outdated WordPress, plugins or themes (the most common way WordPress databases get hacked)
title_hi: Purana WordPress, plugins ya themes (WordPress database hack hone ka sabse aam raasta)
symptoms: which plugins are active on my wordpress from the database
old plugin caused the hack
wordpress version is very old
plugin update nahi kiya tha isliye hack hua kya
purane plugins se site hack hoti hai kya
nulled theme use kar rahe the

पुराने प्लगइन की वजह से साइट हैक हुई
वर्डप्रेस बहुत पुराना है अपडेट नहीं किया
list installed plugins without logging into wp-admin
admin panel khul nahi raha, database se plugins ki list chahiye
we haven't updated wordpress add-ons in years, is that the reason for the hack
never updated the plugins, did that let the hackers in
add-ons purane hain kabhi update nahi kiye
ऐड-ऑन कभी अपडेट नहीं किए, क्या इसी वजह से हैक
प्लगइन सालों से अपडेट नहीं हुए

diagnose.sql: SELECT option_name, LEFT(option_value, 1000) AS value FROM wp_options WHERE option_name IN ('active_plugins', 'template', 'stylesheet', 'db_version', 'siteurl')
diagnose.look_for: active_plugins lists every running plugin; compare each with wordpress.org for updates and known holes; db_version tells the WordPress version range

diagnose.sql: SELECT option_name, LENGTH(option_value) AS size FROM wp_options WHERE option_name LIKE '%\_site\_transient\_update%' OR option_name LIKE '%update\_core%'
diagnose.look_for: update-check data; missing or very old means WordPress hasn't checked for updates in a long time

diagnose.sql: SELECT option_name, LEFT(option_value, 200) AS value FROM wp_options WHERE option_name IN ('recently_activated', 'uninstall_plugins') OR option_name LIKE '%\_plugin\_%version%' ORDER BY option_name LIMIT 50
diagnose.look_for: plugins switched recently, and versions stored by plugins themselves

causes.title_en: Plugins/themes/core not updated after a security fix was released
causes.title_hi: Security fix aane ke baad bhi plugins/themes/core update nahi kiye

causes.title_en: Pirated (nulled) or abandoned plugins/themes, often with backdoors
causes.title_hi: Pirated (nulled) ya band ho chuke plugins/themes, aksar backdoor ke saath

fixes.steps_en: Take a backup, update WordPress core, all plugins and themes, delete inactive ones, and turn on automatic updates for minor and security releases.
fixes.steps_hi: Backup lo, WordPress core, saare plugins aur themes update karo, inactive wale delete karo, aur minor/security releases ke auto updates on karo.

fixes.steps_en: Remove nulled/abandoned items and replace them with versions from wordpress.org or the real vendor; then run the 'prove it's clean' checks and change passwords.
fixes.steps_hi: Nulled/band ho chuke items hatao aur wordpress.org ya asli vendor wale version lagao; phir 'prove it's clean' checks chalao aur passwords badlo.

verify.en: Dashboard > Updates shows nothing pending, active_plugins lists only plugins you recognise, and a security scan is clean.
verify.hi: Dashboard > Updates mein kuch pending nahi, active_plugins mein sirf pehchaane hue plugins hain, aur security scan saaf hai.

test_phrases: we never updated the add-ons on our wordpress site for years, could that be how we got hacked
wordpress ke add-ons saalon se update nahi kiye, kya isi se hack hua
वर्डप्रेस के ऐड-ऑन सालों से अपडेट नहीं किए, क्या इसी से हैक हुआ

title_en: Backups exist but were never tested (will they really restore after a hack?)
title_hi: Backups hain par kabhi test nahi kiye (hack ke baad sach mein restore honge?)
symptoms: how do i know my database backups actually work
backup was empty when we tried to restore
test restore of database backup
backup to ho raha hai par chalta hai ya nahi pata nahi
restore karne gaye to backup kharab nikla
hosting backup pe bharosa kar sakte hain kya
क्या मेरा डेटाबेस बैकअप सच में काम करता है
बैकअप से रिस्टोर किया तो डेटा नहीं आया
backup strategy so ransomware cannot delete them
pg_dump backups have been 0 bytes for weeks
backup same server pe hi rakha hai

diagnose.sql: SHOW VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name IN ('log_bin', 'binlog_format', 'binlog_expire_logs_seconds', 'expire_logs_days')
diagnose.look_for: with log_bin ON you can replay changes after the last backup (point-in-time recovery); OFF means you lose everything since the last dump

diagnose.sql: SELECT TABLE_SCHEMA, ROUND(SUM(DATA_LENGTH + INDEX_LENGTH) / 1024 / 1024, 1) AS size_mb, COUNT(*) AS tables_count FROM information_schema.TABLES WHERE TABLE_SCHEMA NOT IN ('mysql', 'information_schema', 'performance_schema', 'sys') GROUP BY TABLE_SCHEMA
diagnose.look_for: the size and table count a good backup must roughly match; a much smaller backup file is a warning

diagnose.sql: SELECT archived_count, last_archived_wal, last_archived_time, failed_count, last_failed_time FROM pg_stat_archiver
diagnose.look_for: failed_count growing or last_archived_time old = continuous backup is broken

diagnose.sql: SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name IN ('wal_level', 'archive_mode', 'archive_timeout')
diagnose.look_for: archive_mode off = only nightly dumps; no point-in-time recovery

diagnose.sql: SELECT pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size(current_database())) AS db_size, (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname NOT IN ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema')) AS tables_count
diagnose.look_for: what a full restore should bring back

causes.title_en: Backups are made but nobody has ever restored one, so silent failures go unnoticed
causes.title_hi: Backups bante hain par kisi ne kabhi restore karke nahi dekha, to chupchap fail hote rehte hain

causes.title_en: Backups kept on the same server/account the attacker can reach
causes.title_hi: Backups usi server/account par jahan hacker pahunch sakta hai

causes.title_en: Only nightly dumps, no binary log / WAL archive, so a day of data is lost
causes.title_hi: Sirf raat ke dumps, binary log / WAL archive nahi, to ek din ka data jaata hai

fixes.steps_en: Once a month restore the latest backup into a separate test database and compare table counts and a few row counts with production.
fixes.steps_hi: Har mahine latest backup ko alag test database mein restore karo aur production se table count aur kuch row counts milao.

fixes.steps_en: Keep at least one copy off the server, in an account the database server cannot delete from (versioned/immutable storage).
fixes.steps_hi: Kam se kam ek copy server ke bahar rakho, aise account mein jahan se database server delete na kar sake (versioned/immutable storage).

fixes.steps_en: Turn on the binary log (MySQL) or WAL archiving (PostgreSQL) so you can recover to just before the attack.
fixes.steps_hi: Binary log (MySQL) ya WAL archiving (PostgreSQL) on karo taaki hamle se thik pehle tak recover kar sako.

verify.en: A restore test this month succeeded with matching table counts, and one copy lives off the server.
verify.hi: Is mahine ka restore test safal raha aur table counts mile, aur ek copy server ke bahar hai.

test_phrases: we pay for backups every night but no one ever checked if we can get the data back from them
har raat backup hota hai par kisi ne check nahi kiya ki usse data wapas aayega ya nahi
हर रात बैकअप होता है पर किसी ने नहीं देखा कि उससे डेटा वापस आएगा या नहीं

title_hi: Database dobara kabhi hack na ho, iske liye kya karein (security checklist)
symptoms: how to secure my database
database security best practices checklist
harden mysql server
database ko secure kaise kare

postgres ko safe kaise banaye

दोबारा हैक न हो इसके लिए क्या करें
after cleaning the hack what should we change to stay safe
mysql security checklist for production
database protection steps for small business
what should i lock down so this never happens again
steps to protect the db going forward
list of things to make my database safe from hackers

phir kabhi aisa na ho iske liye database mein kya band karein
डेटाबेस को सुरक्षित करने की लिस्ट चाहिए
ताकि ये फिर कभी न हो डेटाबेस में क्या बदलें

diagnose.sql: SHOW VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name IN ('bind_address', 'skip_networking', 'require_secure_transport', 'have_ssl', 'secure_file_priv', 'local_infile', 'log_bin', 'general_log', 'version')
diagnose.look_for: network: local/private only; TLS required; secure_file_priv limited; local_infile OFF; binary log ON; a supported version

diagnose.sql: SELECT GRANTEE, PRIVILEGE_TYPE FROM information_schema.USER_PRIVILEGES WHERE PRIVILEGE_TYPE IN ('SUPER', 'FILE', 'CREATE USER', 'PROCESS', 'SHUTDOWN', 'RELOAD') ORDER BY GRANTEE
diagnose.look_for: admin-level rights only on a few local admin accounts, never on app users or '%' hosts

diagnose.sql: SHOW VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name LIKE 'validate_password%' OR Variable_name LIKE 'simple_password_check%'
diagnose.look_for: a password-strength check should be active

diagnose.sql: SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name IN ('listen_addresses', 'ssl', 'password_encryption', 'log_connections', 'log_statement', 'archive_mode', 'server_version')
diagnose.look_for: listen_addresses not '*' (or firewalled), ssl on, scram-sha-256, connections logged, archiving on, a supported version

diagnose.sql: SELECT rolname, rolsuper, rolcreaterole, rolcreatedb, rolbypassrls, rolcanlogin FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname NOT LIKE 'pg\_%' ORDER BY rolsuper DESC, rolname
diagnose.look_for: only one local superuser; app roles without special attributes

causes.title_en: Reachable from the internet
causes.title_hi: Internet se pahunch mein

causes.title_en: Too many powerful or shared accounts, weak passwords
causes.title_hi: Bahut saare powerful ya shared accounts, kamzor passwords

causes.title_en: No logs, no tested backups, outdated software
causes.title_hi: Logs nahi, test kiye backups nahi, purana software

fixes.steps_en: Database on localhost/private network, port firewalled to the app server, TLS required, no public phpMyAdmin/Adminer.
fixes.steps_hi: Database localhost/private network par, port sirf app server ke liye firewall mein khula, TLS zaroori, public phpMyAdmin/Adminer nahi.

fixes.steps_en: One limited user per app, no remote root/superuser, long unique passwords with a strength check, remove accounts nobody uses.
fixes.steps_hi: Har app ka ek limited user, remote root/superuser nahi, strength check ke saath lambe alag passwords, jo accounts koi use nahi karta unhe hatao.

fixes.steps_en: Log logins and schema changes, keep backups off the server and test a restore monthly, update the database and the app/CMS regularly.
fixes.steps_hi: Logins aur schema changes log karo, backups server ke bahar rakho aur har mahine restore test karo, database aur app/CMS niyamit update karo.

verify.en: Every check above shows the safe value, and the same checks are re-run monthly.
verify.hi: Upar ke har check mein safe value dikhti hai, aur yahi checks har mahine dobara chalte hain.

test_phrases: give me a list of things to lock down on my database so this never happens again
database ko pakka band karne ki list do taaki ye phir kabhi na ho
डेटाबेस को पक्का सुरक्षित करने की लिस्ट दो ताकि ये फिर कभी न हो

title_en: MongoDB wiped and a ransom note left (database open without a password)
title_hi: MongoDB khali ho gaya aur phirauti (ransom) note chhoda (database bina password khula tha)
symptoms: mongodb collections deleted and a README collection asking for bitcoin
my mongo database is empty and there is a ransom message
mongodb hacked warning database
mongo db mein saara data gayab aur bitcoin maang rahe hain
mongodb mein naya database aa gaya READ_ME naam ka
mongo ka data delete karke paise maang rahe hain
मोंगो डीबी का सारा डेटा गायब और बिटकॉइन मांग रहे हैं
मोंगोडीबी हैक हो गया फिरौती का मैसेज
mongodb without authentication exposed on 27017
all my mongo collections replaced by one with a ransom note
mongo db hack hua kya karein
mongo data vanished and a message asks for crypto
mongo database emptied and they want payment in bitcoin
mongo ka data chala gaya aur crypto maang rahe hain
मोंगो का डेटा चला गया और क्रिप्टो मांग रहे हैं
nosql mongo wiped with a pay us note

diagnose.look_for: a database/collection named like README, READ_ME_TO_RECOVER, WARNING or PLEASE_READ that you didn't create; your own databases missing
net.bindIp 0.0.0.0 / bindIpAll and no security.authorization: enabled = anyone could connect without a password
no users at all (auth was never set up) or admin users you don't know

causes.title_en: MongoDB was reachable from the internet with access control off (no password)
causes.title_hi: MongoDB internet se khula tha aur access control band tha (koi password nahi)

fixes.steps_en: Do not pay: in most such attacks the data was never copied, only deleted. Firewall port 27017 now, enable security.authorization and bind to localhost/private IP, create an admin and app users, restore from your last backup, and report it if personal data was exposed.
fixes.steps_hi: Paise mat do: aise zyada hamlon mein data copy hi nahi hua, sirf delete hua. Abhi port 27017 firewall karo, security.authorization on aur localhost/private IP par bind karo, admin aur app users banao, aakhri backup se restore karo, aur personal data tha to report karo.

verify.en: Connecting without a password is refused, the port is not reachable from outside, and your data is back from backup.
verify.hi: Bina password connection mana hota hai, port bahar se nahi khulta, aur backup se data wapas aa gaya.

test_phrases: our mongo data disappeared and someone left a note asking for crypto payment
hamara mongo ka data udd gaya aur koi crypto mein paise maang raha hai
हमारा मोंगो का डेटा उड़ गया और कोई क्रिप्टो में पैसे मांग रहा है

title_en: Elasticsearch indices deleted and a ransom index left (cluster open to the internet)
title_hi: Elasticsearch ke indices delete aur ransom index chhoda (cluster internet par khula)
symptoms: elasticsearch indices got deleted and there is a read_me index
all my elastic indexes are gone
kibana data suddenly missing and a warning index
elasticsearch ke saare index gayab ho gaye
elastic mein read me naam ka index aa gaya bitcoin wala
search data ud gaya elastic se
इलास्टिकसर्च के सारे इंडेक्स गायब हो गए
elasticsearch port 9200 open without password
opensearch cluster wiped with ransom message
elastic hack ho gaya kya karein

diagnose.look_for: an index named like read_me / warning / recover you didn't create, created at the time your data vanished
if this works without credentials (or security is not enabled), the cluster is open to anyone who can reach it
network.host 0.0.0.0 / a public IP on port 9200

causes.title_en: Cluster reachable from the internet with security (authentication) disabled
causes.title_hi: Cluster internet se khula aur security (authentication) band

fixes.steps_en: Do not pay. Block port 9200/9300 in the firewall, turn on security (xpack.security.enabled: true) with passwords and TLS, bind to a private address, then restore from a snapshot or re-index from the main database.
fixes.steps_hi: Paise mat do. Firewall mein port 9200/9300 band karo, security (xpack.security.enabled: true) passwords aur TLS ke saath on karo, private address par bind karo, phir snapshot se restore karo ya main database se re-index karo.

verify.en: An unauthenticated request gets 401, the port is closed to the internet, and your indices are back.
verify.hi: Bina login request ko 401 milta hai, port internet ke liye band hai, aur aapke indices wapas aa gaye.

test_phrases: the search server lost every index overnight and a new one says pay us
search server ke saare index raat mein gaye aur naya index paise maang raha hai
सर्च सर्वर के सारे इंडेक्स रात में गायब, नया इंडेक्स पैसे मांग रहा है

title_en: Redis open to the internet (keys wiped, strange keys, crypto-miner on the server)
title_hi: Redis internet par khula (keys mit gayi, ajeeb keys, server par crypto-miner)

causes.title_en: Redis reachable from the internet without a password (protected mode off)

fixes.steps_en: Firewall port 6379, bind to 127.0.0.1/private IP, keep protected-mode yes, set a strong password/ACL users, rename or disable CONFIG for app users, run Redis as a non-root user; then check the server for unknown cron jobs, SSH keys and processes.

verify.en: From outside the port is closed, commands without a password are refused, and no unknown processes or cron jobs remain.
verify.hi: Bahar se port band hai, bina password commands mana hote hain, aur koi anjaan process ya cron job nahi bacha.

diagnose.sql: SHOW VARIABLES WHERE Variable_name IN ('port', 'socket', 'bind_address', 'skip_networking', 'hostname')
diagnose.look_for: skip_networking ON or bind_address 127.0.0.1 means no other machine can connect; the port the app must use

diagnose.look_for: listen_addresses 'localhost' accepts only local connections; the port the app must use

causes.title_en: The database service is stopped or crashed (often after a reboot or running out of memory/disk)
causes.title_hi: Database service band hai ya crash ho gayi (aksar reboot ya memory/disk khatam hone ke baad)

causes.title_en: The app points to the wrong host or port
causes.title_hi: App galat host ya port par connect kar rahi hai

causes.title_en: The server listens only on localhost (bind_address / listen_addresses / skip_networking)
causes.title_hi: Server sirf localhost par sunta hai (bind_address / listen_addresses / skip_networking)

fixes.steps_en: Start the service (systemctl start mysql|mariadb|postgresql), enable it at boot, then read the server error log for why it stopped (out of memory, disk full, bad config).
fixes.steps_hi: Service start karo (systemctl start mysql|mariadb|postgresql), boot par enable karo, phir server error log padho ki kyun band hua (memory, disk full, galat config).

fixes.steps_en: Put the exact host and port the server reports into the app's config (.env / wp-config.php); 'localhost' and '127.0.0.1' are not always the same (socket vs TCP).
fixes.steps_hi: Server jo host aur port batata hai wahi app ke config (.env / wp-config.php) mein daalo; 'localhost' aur '127.0.0.1' hamesha same nahi (socket vs TCP).

fixes.steps_en: If the app runs on another machine, set bind_address / listen_addresses to the server's private IP (not the whole internet), allow that one app IP in the firewall, restart in a quiet hour.
fixes.steps_hi: Agar app doosri machine par hai to bind_address / listen_addresses ko server ka private IP karo (poora internet nahi), firewall mein sirf app ka IP allow karo, shant time par restart karo.

verify.en: The app connects without 'refused' errors, and the service starts again by itself after a reboot.
verify.hi: App bina 'refused' error ke connect hoti hai, aur reboot ke baad service khud start hoti hai.
